answer.evidence: Rows 1-3 are an orange-brown top band. Row 4 is a lighter front-edge line (#d59147). Rows 5-8 are dark eave shadow (L=50, then 28). This matches the green cabinet reference of a top band, edge line and eave. Below it the front face runs from row 5 to row 43, about 39 rows, in three stacked bays. Each bay has a dark back, a white and blue mattress seen face-on, and a front beam strip (rows 14-15, 26-27, 38-39). The beams are front-facing strips, not top surfaces. No receding side face is drawn, and the silhouette is a constant 16 px wide.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall wooden frame with three stacked bunks. Each bunk has a blue mattress and a white pillow, and the frame carries a dark brown edge. Only 22% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans brown and counts as dark_material_tone, not a black sticker line. It has 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above prop-hedge (9) and comparable to the other references that have a tile measure. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the mattresses and pillows are broken up by highlights and shadow. The frame wood shows about 4 steps and the blue ramp about 3, a little below the 5-6 steps in Beodeul. The palette is small, with 15 distinct colours against 14-40 in the references, and the grain is modest. That is slightly lower than the richest references (well, stall) but in line with the simpler bench and hedge, so a careful artist would accept it beside them.
